question: What does a markdown cell do?

answers.answer: It formats and displays its contents as plain text.
answers.feedback: Correct! It doesn't run its contents as code.

answers.answer: It runs anything inside it via the python language.
answers.feedback: No! That is the job of the code cell.

answers.answer: It runs anything inside it via the MATLAB language.
answers.feedback: No! Matlab and Python are distinctly separate languages.

question: How can you visually distinguish code and markdown cells?

answers.answer: Code cells are greyish, while Markdown cells are typically white or multicolored.
answers.feedback: Yes! Only markdown cells have the ability to color their background as anything. Code cells are strictly greyish.
Although markdown cells are very flexible (they can display things as codescript), in general you'll see code cells consisting of the characteristic blocky text.

answers.answer: Code cells have a [] on their left margin.
answers.feedback: Yes! If not run yet, the bracket will be empty. If run, it will have a number; for example, [3] means that it was the third code cell that was run.

answers.answer: Markdown cells are the outputs of code cells.
answers.feedback: No! Outputs of code cells are typically considered still part of the code cell.
